newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand stabilised by late Wednesday after taking pummelling earlier on foreign selling, dealers said.

At 1455 GMT the currency was at 4.4775/4805 against the dollar compared to 4.4650/4680 late Tuesday, having challenged the 4.4850 level early where it found exporters waiting to lap it up on the cheap.

Local players said it was still unclear if a large London-based long rand/short dollar position - which has kept the rand under pressure and was rumoured to be as large as $300 million - had been completely unwound.
"There's still a few questions out there about that one," said one trader.
Traders called a range of 4.4800-4.4700 for after-hours action.
In cross rate trading, the currency suffered further losses against the yen over the afternoon.
The rand was last at 26.4852/5118 yen from 26.6674/7077 late Tuesday, 0.3801/3804 marks from 0.3798/3802 previously and 7.3359/3453 on sterling from 7.2780/2873 before.
Bond dealers bemoaned the torpid local debt market, with meagre volumes keeping the key R150 bond see-sawing either side of Tuesday's 14.925 close.
In the afternoon, a fall in the U.S. April PPI figure saw the long bond perk up on the back of U.S. debt revitalised by lessened rate hike fears.
The move also was helped by hopes of some local hedging on the back of Deutsche Bank's 2.0 billion rand 20-year eurobond announced earlier.
But the activity was not enough to convince jobbers to stay long ahead of Thursday's settlement deadline as they shoved the bond back into the red at the tail end of official dealings.

"Those U.S. PPI figures that came out...were pretty strong. I thought it (the R150) would have strengthened a bit but then some jobbers got rid of some of their long positions before the carries," said one trader.
Rand weakness also weighed on sentiment.
South Africa is expected to unveil its prroducer price figures at 0900 GMT Thursday. March PPI is forecast to have risen 0.1 percent from February and to 9.7 percent year on year.
Bond Exchange data showed foreigners picked up local debt totalling 626.01 million rand on Tuesday after selling 25.96 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Friday.
Nominal Bond Exchange turnover jumped to 6.24 billion rand on Tuesday from 4.71 billion rand on Monday.
In the money market, three month NCD rates from major banks were unchanged at 16.40 percent offered from Tuesday's level, while 90-day BA rates remained between 15.90 and 15.95 percent.
The Reserve Bank reported the money market shortage fell to 7.493 billion rand on Tuesday from 7.775 billion rand Monday.
